clue.text: One sometimes seen in pool, skilled in key strokes

definitions.text: One sometimes seen in pool, skilled in key strokes

parts.words: One sometimes seen in pool, skilled in key strokes
parts.note: the pool is an office typing pool, not a swimming pool, and the key strokes are on a keyboard rather than in the water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool' and 'strokes' paint a swimmer; the pool is a typing pool and the strokes hit keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Office workers in a typing pool were skilled keyboard operators producing letters.

clue.text: Square cape

definitions.meaning: a famous London square with Nelson's Column
a headland in south-west Spain, scene of Nelson's victory

explanation.walkthrough: Trafalgar Square is in central London; Cape Trafalgar is in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the London plaza and the Spanish headland share the battle's name.

clue.text: Joint cover for boy and girl

explanation.surface: A protective covering shared by a boy and a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap is the bone shielding the knee joint.

clue.text: Slightly mistimed order before fighting starts

definitions.meaning: the call to boxers' helpers to leave the ring before a round

explanation.surface: A command at a boxing match given a little late.
explanation.definitionFit: Off by a few seconds, and the referee's call clearing helpers from the ring.

clue.text: Vaulting ambition may be to keep this up

definitions.text: Vaulting ambition may be to keep this up

parts.words: Vaulting ambition may be to keep this up
parts.note: Macbeth's 'vaulting ambition' becomes the literal aim of a pole vaulter, who wants the horizontal bar to stay on its supports

explanation.surface: A line about ambition echoing Macbeth's 'vaulting ambition'.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'vaulting ambition' comes from Macbeth; here it is read literally, as a pole vaulter's goal of clearing the bar without knocking it down.
explanation.definitionFit: In pole vault and high jump the athlete must clear the horizontal bar without dislodging it.

clue.text: Changed it internally, like 24

definitions.note: the novel at 24 across is titled with this word after it

indicators.note: the word it goes inside the other word

explanation.surface: Editing a text by altering its inner part, as with a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 across is BRIDESHEAD, and Waugh's novel is Brideshead Revisited.
explanation.definitionFit: Waugh's novel title adds this word to the castle's name, so it qualifies 24 like that title.

clue.text: Group containing only one bit of church

definitions.text: Group containing only one bit of church

indicators.note: the word for a group holds the single letter within it
just one letter of the word church is used, its first

explanation.surface: A faction holding just a small part of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts C, the first letter of 'church' (from 'only one bit of'), inside SET; read whole, the clue describes a breakaway body holding part of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakaway religious faction is a body of followers split from a larger denomination.

clue.text: Two pieces of music — A major — one played

definitions.note: Major Barbara is a play by George Bernard Shaw

parts.note: a bar is a measure of music, so two of them

explanation.surface: A music lesson: two passages in A major are performed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A major' looks like a musical key; A is a letter and 'major' belongs with Shaw's play Major Barbara.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's drama Major Barbara is named after its heroine, the Salvation Army officer.

clue.text: Artificial fabric or any alternative

indicators.note: an alternative form of the letters is made

explanation.surface: A choice between synthetic cloth or any other kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' rearranges OR ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic textile made from regenerated cellulose, once called artificial silk.

clue.text: The old students cheer

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
L for learner, so two learners

explanation.surface: Former undergraduates giving a shout.
explanation.walkthrough: L is a learner, from the L-plates of British learner drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A shout of support, as from a cheerleader.

clue.text: Composition in A

definitions.meaning: a piece of writing, as in a newspaper or magazine
the word 'a' is the indefinite ... in grammar

explanation.walkthrough: The capital A looks like a grade or a musical key; it is the grammatical part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A written piece in a journal is so called, and 'a' and 'the' are the grammar's determiners of that name.

clue.text: Governor's boy is beyond wickedness

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is just Governor

indicators.note: one piece comes after, or beyond, the other in the word

explanation.surface: A governor's son has gone past mere wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Governor's' reads as possessive; the 's is 'is' and links to the wordplay. 'is beyond' puts ROY after VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonial ruler governing a province in the monarch's name, as in British India.

clue.text: Finally making large shoe?

definitions.meaning: in the end, after much waiting
a last is the foot-shaped block a cobbler uses, so a shoemaker of big shoes works at a long one

explanation.walkthrough: A last is the wooden form on which a shoe is made; making a large shoe you would be at a long one.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning eventually, after a long wait.

clue.text: Murderer I put in prison

indicators.note: the letter I is placed inside the word for prison

explanation.surface: A killer confesses to having locked someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's first killer, who slew his brother Abel.

clue.text: Having diabolic control

definitions.meaning: a devil taking over a person

explanation.surface: Being in the grip of a demon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ownership of something, and demonic occupation of a person's soul.

clue.text: They help observer see schooners, say

definitions.meaning: a schooner is a large drinking vessel for sherry or beer

explanation.surface: Nautical watchers spotting sailing ships.
explanation.walkthrough: Schooners look like ships for the observer to spot; they are large drinking vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles correct vision, and tumblers or schooners are drinking vessels.

clue.text: Give 'up in sea-storm, full of gloom

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other
a storm tosses the letters about

parts.note: to turn in is to surrender or give up

explanation.surface: Despondent, abandoning hope in a gale at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' rearranges SEA to SAE, and 'in' puts TURNIN inside it, after SA.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy and morose in temperament, from the supposed influence of a planet.

clue.text: Model workers who resisted investment

definitions.meaning: to work like one of these is to work very hard
investment here means a military siege, which the people of Troy held out against for ten years

explanation.surface: Exemplary employees who turned down a financial opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' sounds financial; it is the old military sense, a siege, here the siege of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: People of Troy, proverbial for hard work and for holding out against the Greek siege.

clue.text: When callow youth goes without hot meals?

definitions.text: When callow youth goes without hot meals?

parts.words: When callow youth goes without hot meals?
parts.note: cold dishes of leaves stand for the green, inexperienced years of youth, Shakespeare's phrase from Antony and Cleopatra

explanation.surface: Young people living on cold food.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleopatra calls her 'salad days, when I was green in judgment'; the clue reads the phrase as eating only cold food.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of youthful inexperience, from Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: Describe consequence of close vote

definitions.meaning: a narrow election result often leads to the ballots being tallied again

explanation.surface: Explaining what happens after a tight election.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate an account, and a second tally of ballots after a narrow election.

clue.text: A French' composer initially caught ship from Spain

indicators.note: the first letter of the word caught is taken

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was a French composer

explanation.surface: A French composer at first takes a Spanish vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: C from 'caught' comes first, then A and RAVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fast sailing vessel used by Spanish and Portuguese explorers, like Columbus's Niña.

clue.text: Rifle I sloped as ordered

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier with his rifle at the slope, as commanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' looks like a gun; it is the verb meaning to plunder. 'as ordered' rearranges I SLOPED.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack or plunder, as one might strip a place of valuables.

clue.text: Public appearance outside the House

parts.note: an air is an appearance or manner

explanation.surface: A politician appearing in public outside Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the House' suggests Parliament; it just means any building.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking place outdoors rather than within a building.

clue.text: Fool about, grabbing the King's dagger

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the king's letter inside it
the word for fool is turned round

parts.note: R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: A jester larking around seizes the monarch's knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses KID to DIK, and 'grabbing' puts R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A short Scottish stabbing knife.

clue.text: French artist a saint? Doesn't sound like it

definitions.text: a saint? Doesn't sound like it
definitions.meaning: The patron saint of Wales, but the French painter's name is said dah-VEED, unlike the saint's

explanation.surface: Questioning whether a French painter could be a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: The painter's name is spelt like the Welsh patron saint's but said the French way.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques-Louis David painted The Death of Marat; the spelling matches Wales's patron saint.

clue.text: Castle in Hebrides he adapted

indicators.note: the castle's name sits inside the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A castle in the Scottish isles is adapted by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' looks like the anagram signal, but HEBRIDES HE lacks an A and D; the name runs across 'heBRIDES HE ADapted', marked by 'in'. Brideshead is the fictional house of Waugh's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The great country house of Evelyn Waugh's novel, filmed at Castle Howard.

clue.text: Cart seen in distance overturned

indicators.note: the word for a distance is turned upside down, written backwards in a down light

explanation.surface: A cart upturned some way off.
explanation.definitionFit: A low heavy cart for brewers' barrels.

clue.text: Centre of defence abandoned in French town

indicators.note: the middle letter of the defence word is the one picked
that middle letter is left out

parts.note: an alibi is a defence in court

explanation.surface: A town in France where the central defender went missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre of ... abandoned' drops the middle I from ALIBI.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral city in southern France, birthplace of Toulouse-Lautrec.

clue.text: He scored every season

parts.note: scored means wrote music, and every season means all four seasons, so this is the composer of a famous set of concertos

explanation.surface: A sportsman who found the net in every campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scored' and 'season' suggest a footballer; the scoring is musical and the seasons are the Four Seasons concertos.
explanation.definitionFit: Venetian Baroque composer of The Four Seasons violin concertos.

clue.text: Woodcutter covers a distance in China by degrees

parts.note: the li is a Chinese unit of distance
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree, so two of them

explanation.surface: A woodsman travels a long way across China step by step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by degrees' looks like 'gradually'; it gives two BA degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: The poor woodcutter hero of the Arabian Nights tale of the forty thieves.

clue.text: Cure mild, disorder — this is instrumental

indicators.note: the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Treating a minor illness, presented as a useful remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' looks medical alongside 'cure'; it rearranges CURE MILD.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed instrument struck with small hammers, so it is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Artist removing end on the way in

explanation.surface: A painter taking away the last part of the entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing end' drops the final S from INGRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres, French Neoclassical painter.
